description_en: The five-bayed Laganakhela Phalcā is managed by the Laganakhela Bhajana Maṇḍala, a local committee. It is occupied by four shops. This five-bayphalcāhas been converted into four small shops and is no longer used for religious activities. The southern, shorter side of Laganakhela Phalcā has been closed off with a brick wall and its interior has been divided up into four rooms. All of the previously open bays have been adapted so they can be closed using boards and top-hinged panels. The five plinths have been plastered with cement and are now used to display the shops' wares. The Laganakhela Phalcā still retains its traditionaljhĩgaṭīroof, but this has been badly damaged and is now (in 2019) covered with a tarpaulin. The Laganakhela Bhajana Maṇḍala collects rent under the pretext of looking after the phalcā, however, it is obvious that thephalcāhas been neglected and that its roof is in dire need of repair. There is neither a record of an activeguṭhīnor is there any inscription with which to date the monument. A structure dating from the Rāṇā period is located to its west.
description_ne: लगनखेल बसपार्कको पश्चिममा यो फल्चा अवस्थित छ । बाटोको सतहबाट पाँच तहको पेटीमाथि बनेको फल्चामा ५ कवलहरु रहेका छन् । फल्चाको निर्माण तथा जीर्णोद्धारबारे जानकारी दिने कुनै अभिलेख प्राप्त छैन । बुङ्गद्यःलाई न्हवं (महास्नान) गराइँदा, बुङ्गद्यःको रथ लगनखेल ल्याइँदा र रथलाई लगनखेलस्थित माँसिमा परिक्रमा गराइँदा यस फल्चामा पाटन कुमारीलाई विराजमान गराउने परम्परा चल्दै आएको छ । यस बाहेक फल्चामा अन्य कुनै धार्मिक एवं सांस्कृतिक गतिविधि भएगरेको पाइँदैन । हाल फल्चामा पसल खोली कवलहरुमा काठका ढोकाहरु हालिएका छन् । फल्चामा कुमारीलाई विराजमान गराइने दिन पसलका सामान सारी कुमारीलाई साँघुरो ठाँउ खाली गर्ने गरिएको देखिन्छ । फल्चाको भाडा असुली तथा रेखदेखको कार्य लगनखेल भगन मण्डलले गर्दै आएको छ ।

historical_events.event_description: The area behind thisphalcāis calledbāhāḥ,where one can see several Buddhist statues and Hindu shrines. The organisation managing thephalcāis named Laganakhela Bhajana Maṇḍala. It has organisedbhajanain thisbāhāḥfor the last 40 years and is also responsible for renting shop space.

In the 1970s the Lagankhel area was reconstructed and a public bus station was built. At that time homeless people from the area started using thephalcāas their shelter. To prevent this, the residents of Lagankhel, Thati and Taṃgaḥ decided to rent thephalcāout to shops. According to an elderly man living in Thati Ṭola, the rent collected from thephalcāwas used to install street lights in the area.
Due to the continuous rainfall of the monsoon season, the roof was damaged and began to leak water under thephalcā. The roof was repaired once the monsoon ended.
